artifacts.synopsis: TE Robert Hopper challenged James River Presbytery's restriction on teaching and preaching about present-day prophecy and tongues. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that presbytery may limit such teaching for the welfare of the church when it determines the views threaten the church's peace or purity, while declining to issue a comprehensive doctrinal ruling.

artifacts.synopsis: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.

artifacts.title: Court's authority to investigate before filing charges under BCO 32-2

matches.evidence: The CCB found the proposed amendment to BCO 32-2 clarifying a court's investigative authority both in conflict with and ambiguous in relation to the BCO.

artifacts.title: Proposed Revision of BCO 59 Marriage Language and Consent

matches.evidence: The CCB found Calvary Presbytery's overture to revise BCO 59 in conflict with the Constitution, as proposed changes to marriage publication and consent conflicted with BCO Preliminary Principle 7, BCO 11-2, BCO 29-1, and WCF 20.2.
